what: THE FRONTIER PROJECTOR, COMPILED FROM CHARTERS AND QUESTIONS — the cairnmap move applied to the frontier. Gathers every charter's filed_edges plus the open-*.json questions from CairnCommons/questions/ and compiles one surface. Zero inference, mutates nothing. A view, not a device.
why: Filed at the creation of the open-questions lane (decisions/2026-08-01-edges-become-open-questions): nothing yet compiled every charter's filed_edges into a single frontier view. The frontier was scattered across 30+ charters and unmeasurable without reading each one. The same design that cairnmap applies to the help surface (gather, project, derive) is applied here to the frontier — so a mind asking 'what is the edge of this system' gets one compiled answer, not 30 files to open. The held-what-next-review script is its first consumer.
invoke: `cairn edges` (the full frontier). Import: `from cairn.tools.edges import edges`. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/edges/proofs/test_edges.py` (exit 0 = green).
node_class: code-seam — the projection code is the code, one address.
how_it_learns: It doesn't, because it is a derivation — regenerate -> current. What learns is the charter corpus and the question corpus underneath it.
entry: cairnmap (the gather/project pattern, the CAIRN_ROOTS_PARENT seam for proof isolation).
filed_edges: (a) NO TICKER YET — owes state/history sidecars when tickets resume.
(b) THE WHAT-NEXT CONSUMER IS NOT WIRED — the held-what-next-review script should call this rather than walking charters itself.
owner: CC owns the projection code (cairn/tools/edges/ + bin/cmd/edges) and its proof.
traces_to: Law 1 (the frontier scattered across 30+ charters is re-derived every session; compile it once)
Law 5 (intent at every address — this shows the edges beside the code, compiled into one surface)
Law 7 (a non-string edge is a RED in the surface, loud at the reader)
